- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py
  Line or code reference: 320 (also root twin at the same line)
  Problem: `_parse_time(commit["commit"]["committer"]["date"])` is the only remaining unguarded call site of the newly-hardened `_parse_time`. The round-1 change makes `_parse_time` raise `ValueError` for any timestamp without a UTC offset, but this caller has no try/except. A committer date without an offset would propagate to `main()` and become `action: retry`, skipping the stuck-head check.
  Why it fails at runtime: In practice, GitHub always returns timezone-aware committer dates, so the path is unreachable. The pre-existing code had the same fragility (a naive datetime would raise `TypeError` on the subtraction at line 321, not ValueError), so this is not a regression. The PR is correct in only fixing the two paths the team identified (the hold-age call site and the claim-lease call site). A future hardener wrapping line 320 in `_hours_since` would close the gap, but introducing that change here would expand scope beyond the issue and the round-2 review already accepted this surface.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py
  Line or code reference: 244-253 (also root twin)
  Problem: `if parsed.tzinfo is None or parsed.utcoffset() is None:` is redundant. In Python's datetime contract, `parsed.utcoffset()` already returns `None` when `parsed.tzinfo` is `None`, so the first clause subsumes the second. Both branches raise the same `ValueError` with the same message; the simplification is purely cosmetic.
  Why it fails at runtime: It does not. The new behavior is correct: naive datetimes (no tzinfo) and tz-aware-but-no-offset values both raise. Round-2 review noted this as well.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py
  Line or code reference: 281-296 (the new fresh-hold vs stale-hold branch in `check_pr`)
  Problem: The fresh-hold branch's `reason` string does not include the `; labels: ...` suffix that the stale-hold branch appends from `stale_hold_labels`. Operators who grep logs for the held state and find no label annotation may not realize a blocking label is present but outranked by the hold per the documented #5667 contract.
  Why it fails at runtime: It does not. The freshness ordering (held wins over labels when younger than the bound) is the documented #5667 contract, not a regression. The asymmetry is by design.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- README.md, agents.md, CLAUDE.md, workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md, .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md, changelog.d/5927-bound-plain-mode-hold.md
  Line or code reference: README.md:92 and :1473-1483; agents.md:1020-1028 and :1063-1070; CLAUDE.md:2125-2135
  Problem: The operator-facing docs explain the bound ("a hold at least `CLAUDE_FIX_HOLD_MAX_HOURS` old is handed back") but do not name the renewal semantics: a trusted author can post a fresh hold before the bound elapses and reset the 24-hour clock, as codified in `test_a_newer_hold_restarts_the_limit`. The plan's AD-5 accepts the risk and `docs/implement-plan/issue-5927-bound-plain-mode-hold.md` (Notes section) records it, but README/CLAUDE.md/agents.md do not. An operator reading only the operator-facing docs may believe a stray or forged hold "cannot park the project for good" without realizing the same author can keep posting holds every 24h.
  Why it fails at runtime: It does not. The bound still ends an indefinite wait from a single marker, and the renewal identity is already trusted enough to push, close, or merge the PR. The information gap is between operator docs and the progress log only.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
